name: Northwest Ridge

pitch_detail.notes: From the grassy gully above Thumbtack Rock, start up the gully to the left of the treed saddle. Gain the ridge and cross over it to belay from trees on its south side.

From the trees, scramble down and to the left, below a chimney-like feature with a chockstone at its top. It cannot be seen from the belay but is obvious once you are across. Climb to the base of the chockstone.

Work around and then over the chockstone onto the ridge proper. Higher up there is a hard-to-protect move up a small vertical face of poor-quality rock. Belay at a flat spot with trees on the right side of the ridge.
Continue left and regain the crest. Steep direct lines off the crest are loose and harder than the route grade, so stick to the easier ridge line; the rock quality is poor throughout.
Run-out ridge climbing continues past a false summit to the true summit, often simul-climbed. For the descent, go south over the false summits to a slung tree in the second gully heading east.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 3, single rope, down the drippy, dank chimney.
rappel_detail.anchor: slings and rap rings on a tree
rappel_detail.station: The marked south-facing gully (the southern chimney) south of the summit, reached by traversing back past the false summits; the anchor is a tree rigged with slings and rings at its top.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 3, single rope, to the foot of the chimney.
rappel_detail.anchor: slings and rings on a tree or chockstone

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 3 of 3, down the steep, narrow snow finger below the chimney, back to the basin.
rappel_detail.anchor: slings at the head of the snow finger
hazards: Seasonal snow: early in the year this is steep snow; later it may be loose rock and scree. Carry extra webbing and rap rings, since the slings are replaced only by passing parties.
rappel_detail.station: The foot of the chimney, above the snow finger.

rappels: 3 rappels from the slung tree in the marked gully south of the summit (the second gully heading east past the false summits): two in the chimney, one down the snow finger, then scree back to Thumbtack Rock
descent_text: From the true summit, traverse south across a series of false summits until reaching a tree rigged with rappel anchors at the second gully encountered heading east. Make multiple rappels down this gully to reach the East Face proper, then descend scree slopes back to Thumbtack Rock and the standard approach path.
approach: Follow the East Face approach to the 'Thumbtack Rock' landmark, then head right up a grassy gully over the ridge toward the start of the Northwest Ridge.
overview: A longer, sustained 5.7 ridge climb on Chair Peak, following the crest over false summits with a mix of solid and notably loose rock — the longest documented rock route on the peak by pitch count.
beta: This is a 6-pitch, 1,000 ft (303 m), Grade II, 5.7 trad route reached via the East Face approach to 'Thumbtack Rock' before angling right over the ridge. It has a low average rating (2/5 stars) reflecting run-out climbing and poor rock quality in places.
gear: Alpine rack (nuts + cams, small sizes emphasized)
